display.purpose: Two uses only: the aggregate rating number and the large step numerals in the dark section.

headline.purpose: Every section heading and the closing CTA heading.

title.purpose: The product name (H1) and the modal title. Deliberately smaller than Headline — see The Shelf Label Rule.

lead.purpose: Section leads, the product subhead, and the closing CTA body.

body.purpose: Prose columns at 16px. Denser contexts use the body-sm and body-xs steps rather than overriding this one.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, fieldset legends, trust titles and spec group headers at 12px. The 11px variant is label-sm.

mono.purpose: Machine-set values only: the primary CTA label, the price band, placeholder captions, the SKU and inline code. Never a heading or a sentence.

body-sm.purpose: 15px step: spec values, review bodies, FAQ answers, modal copy. The densest sans reading size.

body-xs.purpose: 14px step: card blurbs, trust item bodies, the small nav CTA label.

meta.purpose: 13px step: rating link, price terms, review meta, spec labels, footer links.

label-sm.purpose: 11px tracked uppercase: announcement bar, card flags, modal metadata, placeholder captions.

price.purpose: 18px monospace: the salary band. The only mono step above the CTA label.

shadows.name: object-lift
shadows.purpose: Soft ambient lift for discrete objects resting on a ground: project cards, review cards, the specs table.

shadows.name: object-lift-hover
shadows.purpose: Project card hover, paired with translateY(-2px).

shadows.name: press-affordance
shadows.purpose: Hard graphic shadow belonging to the primary CTA alone, always paired with a 1px solid #000 border. Never extend it to a second element.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Every hover and selection transition: background-color, color, border-color, box-shadow. Not motion — state feedback — so it survives prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: skip-link
motion.purpose: The skip link dropping into view on focus. Positional, so it is removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: card-rise
motion.purpose: The only positional motion in the layout, on project card hover. Removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Colour and shadow transitions stay; the card rise and skip-link slide go. The page-level smooth scroll is triggered from JavaScript and reads the preference directly via matchMedia — CSS scroll-behavior cannot reach a scrollIntoView call that passes behavior explicitly.

browserSurfaces.name: selection
browserSurfaces.purpose: 8.78:1 on both light and navy sections, so one rule covers the page.

browserSurfaces.name: color-scheme
browserSurfaces.purpose: Declared on :root so UA scrollbars, form controls and default focus rings render against a light page.

browserSurfaces.name: modal-scrollbar
browserSurfaces.purpose: The quick-look panel is the only internally scrollable surface.

browserSurfaces.name: tabular-nums
browserSurfaces.purpose: On the rating breakdown so the 5-to-1 rail and its counts hold register as values change.

components.name: Primary CTA
components.description: The signature pill: Attention Blue fill, navy label, pure-black hairline, hard graphic shadow. Used in all three CTA placements; label is always 'Add to team'.

components.css: .ds-pills { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(120px, 1fr)); gap: 8px; } .ds-pill { display: block; cursor: pointer; padding: 13px 14px; border: 1.5px solid rgba(2,32,68,.20); border-radius: 8px; background: transparent; color: var(--ink, #022044); transition: border-color .15s, background-color .15s; } .ds-pill:hover { border-color: var(--accent, #9dc1f3); } .ds-pill__in { position: absolute; opacity: 0; width: 0; height: 0; } .ds-pill__lb { display: block; font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.3; } .ds-pill:has(.ds-pill__in:checked) { border: 2px solid var(--accent, #9dc1f3); background: rgba(157,193,243,.1); padding: 12.5px 13.5px; } .ds-pill:has(.ds-pill__in:focus-visible) { outline: 2px solid var(--ink, #022044); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Project Card
components.description: The quick-look trigger. A full-card button with a hatched image frame, a flex body whose cue is pushed to the bottom so unequal cards still align, and a 2px rise on hover.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; width: 280px; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; background: #ffffff; border: 0; border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08); overflow: hidden; color: var(--ink, #022044); font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif; transition: box-shadow .15s, transform .15s; } .ds-card:hover { box-shadow: 0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.12); transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-card:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink, #022044); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-card__frame { position: relative; display: block; aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; border-radius: 10px 10px 0 0; background: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, #dbe6f5 0 9px, #eef4fc 9px 18px); } .ds-card__cap { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); font: 700 11px 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; color: rgba(2,32,68,.75); background: #fff; padding: 6px 10px; border-radius: 4px; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-card__body { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 7px; flex: 1; padding: 18px; } .ds-card__flag { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 2px; text-transform: uppercase; color: rgba(2,32,68,.70); } .ds-card__title { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.35; } .ds-card__blurb { font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.5; color: rgba(2,32,68,.70); } .ds-card__cue { margin-top: auto; padding-top: 14px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 1px; text-transform: uppercase; }

narrative.overview:
Commerce grammar played absolutely straight. Every convention of a direct-to-consumer product detail page is present at full retail fidelity — breadcrumb, gallery with thumb rail, buy box, variant radios, trust bar, ingredient table, star-rating breakdown with distribution bars, quick-look modal, closing CTA block — and not one of them is winked at. The product happens to be a person. Nothing in the visual system acknowledges that. The humour, to the extent there is any, is that everything is exactly precise.

The system is inherited rather than invented. It follows reference/brand-guide.md, the documented visual system of a real DTC supplement brand, adopted 2026-09-13. That inheritance is the argument: a page that merely resembles a storefront would read as pastiche, so this one reproduces a real one's palette logic, type scale, button anatomy and section rhythm closely enough to survive inspection. Two deviations are deliberate and documented in the stylesheet header, both taken for contrast: Attention Blue never carries text on a light ground, and the primary CTA's label is navy rather than white.

This is the incumbent implementation, accurately captured, not permanent law. The palette and type may eventually give way to the person's own identity. Until they do, treat everything here as binding — the page's whole credibility rests on looking built rather than assembled, and drift is the failure mode. Density is retail-moderate: generous vertical section rhythm, tight component interiors, hairlines instead of boxes, and a hard ceiling of 1100px on content width so the page reads as a column rather than a dashboard.
keyCharacteristics: Navy anchors authority; a single pale blue carries every point of attention
Flat surfaces, hairline rules, and background alternation instead of shadow scaffolding
One pill CTA with a black hairline and a hard graphic shadow — the only pressable-looking object on the page
Monospace reserved for machine-set values: price, CTA label, captions, codes
Native HTML doing the structural work — <details name>, <dialog>, real radio groups, real <table>
Every image slot is a hatched placeholder until real assets exist, and looks deliberately unfinished rather than fake

rules.name: The Fill-Only Rule
rules.body: Attention Blue never carries text on a light ground. It appears as a fill, a border, a numeral on navy, or an eyebrow on navy — never as body copy, link text, or a heading on paper. #9dc1f3 on #FAFAF8 is roughly 1.7:1 and fails at any size.

rules.name: The Navy Label Rule
rules.body: The primary CTA's label is Authority Navy, not white. This is a documented deviation from the source brand guide, taken because white on #9dc1f3 measures about 1.8:1. Navy on the same fill clears AA comfortably. If the CTA fill ever changes, the label colour is re-derived from measurement, never inherited.

rules.name: The Never-Twice Rule
rules.body: No two consecutive full-width sections share a background. The flow runs paper → paper-alt → paper → paper-alt → navy → paper → paper-alt → paper → navy. Adding a section means re-checking its neighbours, not appending.

rules.name: The Navy Punctuation Rule
rules.body: Navy appears in the body flow exactly twice: once mid-page (How it works) and once at the close, where the CTA block and footer bar run continuous with no seam between them. A third navy block would turn punctuation into a pattern and flatten the page.

rules.name: The Shelf Label Rule
rules.body: The product name is set smaller than the section headings above and below it — Title tops out at 36px, Headline at 44px. This is correct and intentional. Real product pages do not set the product name as a hero; the buy box is a dense information block, not a title card. Enlarging the H1 is the single fastest way to make this page stop reading as commerce.

rules.name: The Mono Reserve Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono appears only where a storefront prints a value rather than a sentence: the price band, the primary CTA label, placeholder captions, the SKU, and code. It never sets a heading, a body paragraph, or a label. The small nav CTA explicitly opts back into the sans face because at 36px height the tracked monospace reads as a system alert.

rules.name: The Two-Weight Rule
rules.body: Type is 400 or 700. Weights 500 and 600 appear in exactly three places (trust badges, bar labels, the FAQ question) and are inherited from the source guide. Do not introduce a fourth weight to create a new tier — use size and colour.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: New surfaces get a background and a hairline, not a shadow. If a thing needs to feel separated, change its ground (paper-card on paper-alt) or give it a 1px line border.

rules.name: The Two Idioms Rule
rules.body: Object lift and press affordance never mix, and neither is extended to a new element without a reason stronger than "it looked flat." Adding the hard CTA shadow to a second element destroys the buy action's uniqueness; adding a soft shadow to a section destroys the flatness that makes cards read as objects.

narrative.antiReference: It must not look AI-generated. That is the test every change is measured against, and it is why the don'ts are specific rather than tasteful. A generated page announces itself through a small, recognisable set of moves; this page's credibility depends on containing none of them.
dos: Do keep the section background alternation intact (paper → paper-alt → navy) and re-check neighbours when inserting a section — see The Never-Twice Rule.
Do reserve Attention Blue for fills, borders, on-navy text and active states — see The Fill-Only Rule.
Do re-derive a label colour from measured contrast whenever a fill changes, the way the navy CTA label was derived.
Do use native elements for behaviour that has one — <details name> for the accordion, <dialog> for the modal, a real radio group for the variant selector, a real <table> for specs.
Do compensate padding when a border thickens on selection, so nothing shifts.
Do set new type at 400 or 700 and create tiers with size and colour instead of new weights.
Do keep the product name below section-heading scale — see The Shelf Label Rule.
Do let hatched frames stay visibly unfinished. A placeholder that looks like a placeholder is honest; a stock photo standing in for real work is not.
donts: Don't enlarge the H1 into a hero, centre the buy box, or introduce a full-bleed opening statement. The moment the first viewport reads as a portfolio instead of a product page, the entire premise is gone.

Don't add a gradient of any kind to a surface, a heading, or a button. The only gradients in this system are the two hatched placeholders, and they are flat-stepped diagonals standing in for missing images — not decoration. Gradient text and mesh backgrounds are the clearest generated-UI tell there is.

Don't add scroll-triggered reveals, staggered fade-ins, blur-in text, or a floating gradient orb. Motion here is limited to 150ms colour and shadow transitions on hover, a 2px card rise, and the skip link — and prefers-reduced-motion zeroes all of it.
Don't introduce emoji, generic icon-library glyphs, or coloured circular icon badges. The two checkmarks on this page are CSS content: '✓' in navy, and that is the whole icon system.

Don't soften the geometry toward uniform large radii. Radius is a role signal — 40px means "press this," 10px means "this is a card" — and flattening them to one friendly value erases the distinction.
Don't give a second element the hard rgba(0,0,0,.33) 0 4px 4px CTA shadow, or add soft shadows to sections. See The Two Idioms Rule.
Don't treat the commerce framing as a joke in the visual layer — no comic faces, no oversized badges, no ironic styling. Straighter, never sillier.
Don't use pure black or pure white as a text colour. Navy is the ink; Paper is the on-dark. The single #000 on this page is the CTA's border.
Don't add a third navy section to the body flow — see The Navy Punctuation Rule.
standingExceptions: Inter as the primary face reads as an overused, generated-UI-adjacent default. It is kept because it is the source brand guide's own documented fallback for ABC Social, which is licensed and unavailable. If those faces are ever licensed — or if the page moves to the person's own identity — replace Inter rather than defending it. Do not swap it for another popular grotesque; that trades the justification for nothing.

The repeating-gradient hatch is a generated-UI signature in general and a deliberate placeholder idiom here. It is correct only while the image slots are genuinely empty. The moment real imagery lands in content.json, .frame--has-image clears the hatch and the exception retires with it.
